name: Alila Marea Beach Resort Encinitas
positioning: Adult-focused Alila beach resort on the bluffs above South Ponto State Beach in Encinitas, built in natural stone and warm woods with coastal views from nearly every room
best_for: Couples and adults wanting a quiet coastal escape
Surfers and guests who want beach, surf and wellness experiences

facts.text: The resort is steps from the sand, historic Highway 101 and the coastal town of Encinitas, and blends into the bluffs in an eco design.
The resort is designed to echo the surrounding coastal bluff, beach and ocean, framed by natural stone, warm woods and clean lines.
Nearly every room has coastal views.
Occupancy is limited to two people per room to keep the atmosphere tranquil.
Some rooms have an oversized patio with a private firepit and seating.
Each room has a rack for hanging wetsuits.
Spa Alila treatments use minerals and botanicals sourced from the natural landscape.
Seaside Intention Yoga leads guests through mindful movement and an intention-setting exercise using cobblestones on Ponto Beach.
Guests can explore Leucadia, Encinitas, Carlsbad and Cardiff-by-the-Sea on electric-assist bikes.
Part of the cost of The Endless Wave surf experience supports the Rob Machado Foundation, which promotes clean oceans and drinking water.
Solar power preheats the pool and water.
VAGA Restaurant & Bar serves coastal cuisine with sweeping ocean views.

highlights.text: South Ponto State Beach is steps from the resort, and a Beach Concierge provides beach chairs, beach games and surfboards.
The Endless Wave surf experience offers expert instructors, demo boards and hidden breaks.
Spa Alila offers wellness experiences including breathwork, astrology consultations and sound healing sessions.
The Grandview Suite has picture windows overlooking Batiquitos Lagoon, floor-to-ceiling windows facing the Pacific, and a double-sided fireplace opening to a patio.
Large-scale works by artist in residence Aaron Chang hang in the resort, and surfboard wall panels by local board shaper Brian Szymanski decorate The Pocket.

considerations.text: The resort is tailored for adults and caters to adults and couples more than younger generations.
The local stretch of Pacific beach can be rockier than others, so a chair is more useful than a towel.
The hotel does not offer self-parking.
